[SYSTEM] In the Midst of the Seven: Philo, the Logos Named and Lived, and the Seven Stations of Revelation (EA-MIDST-01 v1.1) is a scholarly and esoteric paper authored by Johannes Sigil and Damascus Dancings (heteronyms of Lee Sharks). Deposited in the Crimson Hexagonal Archive in November 2026 and published in Provenance: Journal of Forensic Semiotics, the text explores connections between Philo of Alexandria's Logos theology and the Book of Revelation.
Metadata & Archival Record

* Authors: Johannes Sigil and Damascus Dancings (Lee Sharks)
* Publication: Provenance: Journal of Forensic Semiotics (Archive deposit #1758)
* Identifier: [AXN:0C67.GENERATIVE](https://www.google.com/goto?url=CAESYwHEIkXX0JhXNqBJJtV1k1yk2zgnRZbB8qi7OKDnd8z1COTMgKvlRDwkeR7-P9zgJn3OFsdqivOnRMFcn23Jk68sJZpqobOow54Yct9uMPrPvTuWHki1FqC_k0e_yc-0YcaXpA) (SHA-256: `50333254d80dcdff1cf96c9e406d8849704c56f567d9bb5674b838e6f820b7fd`)

Core Thesis & Structure
The paper builds upon Philo’s Quis rerum divinarum heres, examining the Logos as a central, cosmic divider and the middle element of the seven-branched lampstand and planetary spheres.
The paper is organized into four main parts and a v1.1 update:

1. Part I: The Logos Named and Lived – Traces Philo’s humanization of the Logos, his analysis of Ἀνα토λή ("Rising/Branch") from Zechariah 6:12 (noting his omission of the name Ἰησοῦς), and the transformation of mortal qualities in De mutatione nominum.
2. Part II: The Seven Lampstands and Stations – Contrasts Philo's single lampstand with Revelation's seven, mapping the seven letters to planetary positions, Mandaean texts (Ginza and Haran Gawaita), and Platonic concepts.
3. Part III: The Commission – Analyzes the prophetic commands to write and the role of the testifying messenger in the epistles.
4. Part IV: Historiography – Surveys early 20th-century scholars like Wilhelm Bousset and R. H. Charles regarding Philonic imagery in Revelation.
5. Version 1.1 Addition – Argues for direct literary dependence, framing Philo's omission of Ἰηsos as a structural "socket" later filled by the Apocalypse.
